lead.headline: Flat start to bank-earnings week as oil tops $106 and yields stay near 24-year highs
lead.dek: Index levels are Friday's close. Stocks trade normally on Columbus Day, but the cash Treasury market is shut and no US data is due.
body: Wall Street closed Friday higher (S&P 500 +0.59%, Dow +0.83%, Nasdaq +0.64%), with the S&P and Nasdaq near last week's record highs. Futures were flat on Monday and CNBC reported a little-changed open, with Micron leading chips lower.

The pressure points are rates and oil. The 10-year yield sits near 5.25% after touching about 5.37% last Wednesday, the highest since 2002. Brent rose 1.2% to $106.19 after weekend Houthi strikes on Riyadh airport and tanker attacks near Hormuz. Trump's Russian diesel deal hit diesel futures, not crude.
Watch for the bank results on Tuesday (JPM, GS, C, WFC) and September CPI on Wednesday, forecast at 3.6% y/y. Crypto stays soft, with BTC down about 4% on the week.

side.headline: Q3 season starts Tuesday with JPMorgan, Goldman, Citi and Wells Fargo
side.summary: Consensus EPS: JPM $5.93, GS $13.04, C $2.65, WFC $1.85; J&J ($2.51) and UnitedHealth ($4.12) also report before Tuesday's open. UBS says options are pricing the largest earnings-day moves since Covid.

side.headline: CPI Wednesday is the week's macro test
side.summary: September headline CPI is forecast at +0.6% m/m and 3.6% y/y (prior 3.4%), with core at 2.5% y/y. PPI and retail sales follow on Thursday, and no US data is due today because of the holiday.

side.headline: Fed after its September hike: Waller, Bowman, then Chair Warsh on Friday
side.summary: Cleveland Fed's Hammack said rates need to rise beyond 3.75-4%, and the next FOMC (Oct 27-28) is discussing a second hike. Governor Waller speaks Tuesday, Bowman on Wednesday and Thursday, and Chair Warsh on Friday.

events.text: Columbus Day: NYSE/Nasdaq open, US cash bond market closed (SIFMA), no US economic data
IMF-World Bank meetings begin in Bangkok (through Oct 18); EU expected to approve its largest Russia sanctions package
Earnings: JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, Citi, Wells Fargo, J&J, UnitedHealth; Fed's Waller speaks Tuesday

picks.name: Salesforce
picks.catalyst: BofA double-upgraded the stock to Buy from Underperform and raised its target to $285 from $160. Shares rose about 4% premarket.
picks.bull: BofA argues AI will make customers more dependent on Salesforce, not disrupt it. A sell-side reversal this sharp can draw follow-through buying if the gap holds.
picks.bear: Gap-and-fade risk in a market where 5%+ yields weigh on software valuations. Wells Fargo cut Adobe to Underweight the same day, so the sector call isn't unanimous.
picks.invalidation: Daily close back below $229.13 (gap fully filled)

picks.name: First Solar
picks.catalyst: Truist upgraded the stock to Buy from Hold and raised its target to $270 from $229. CNBC notes it has lost about a third of its value this year.
picks.bull: A beaten-down US-made solar name gets an upgrade with about 50% implied upside to target. Watch for a base-building reversal.
picks.bear: High rates hurt solar project financing, and the downtrend this year has been persistent. One upgrade may not be enough to turn it.
picks.invalidation: Daily close below $177.82 after the upgrade (catalyst rejected)

picks.name: Biogen
picks.catalyst: JPMorgan upgraded it to Overweight and raised its target to $300 from $210, citing a promising pipeline of catalysts expected by 2027 beyond Leqembi. Shares rose about 2% premarket.
picks.bull: Pipeline readouts could re-rate the stock beyond Alzheimer's. Defensive healthcare also offers some cover if CPI or yields knock growth stocks.
picks.bear: Pipeline timing runs to 2027, so this is a slow catalyst. Multiple sclerosis franchise erosion continues, and clinical risk is binary.
picks.invalidation: Close below the pre-upgrade level (Friday close) would negate the catalyst

news.headline: Chips lead tech lower at the open; Micron down about 2%
news.summary: Micron, SanDisk and Intel traded lower early on rotation out of high-valuation tech, while Nvidia held near flat. Separately, Nvidia is reported to be in early talks to acquire or deepen its stake in Reflection AI.

news.headline: Five big banks, two days: can trading offset higher yields?
news.summary: JPM, GS, C and WFC report Tuesday, with BAC and Morgan Stanley on Wednesday. Investors will watch whether strong trading revenue offsets funding-cost and credit pressure from a 5%+ 10-year yield.

news.headline: Brent climbs to $106 as Saudi attacks outweigh Russian diesel deal
news.summary: Brent rose 1.2% to $106.19 by 11:24 GMT, its highest since Sept. 29, after Houthi strikes on Riyadh airport and tanker attacks near Hormuz. Goldman raised its December Brent forecast to $90 and estimates a risk premium of just over $20.

news.headline: Upgrades: CRM, FSLR, BIIB, TMUS. Downgrades: ADBE, HUBS, GDDY, PLTR
news.summary: Wells Fargo cut Adobe to Underweight (target $225) and Barclays cut HubSpot to Equal Weight. Raymond James upgraded T-Mobile to Outperform after its 13% drop, and Evercore started Robinhood at Outperform with a $130 target.

news.headline: SpaceX's $8B spectrum buy rattles carriers, lifts tower stocks
news.summary: SpaceX agreed to buy Grain Management's 800 MHz portfolio for about $8 billion to power Starlink Mobile. T-Mobile, Verizon and AT&T fell 8.5-13% on Friday while Crown Castle, SBA and American Tower rose 7-16%.

news.headline: With the Clarity Act stalled, the SEC and CFTC write the rules
news.summary: The SEC has issued an innovation exemption for tokenized-equity trading and proposed crypto custody rules, and the CFTC is seeking comment on leveraged retail crypto. Spot trading still lacks full federal oversight.

avoid.reason: Wells Fargo downgraded it to Underweight (target $225, below Friday's $242.27), and it traded about 2.6% lower early. It's a negative catalyst in software as yields stay above 5%.

It's up about 4% on a media report, not confirmed by either company, that Anthropic is its unnamed cloud customer, with no terms disclosed. It's still below its 50-day average (~$41.72). Chasing an unverified headline is high risk.
Micro-cap premarket spikes (+100-190%) at around $2-3 a share with no clear catalyst. These are penny stocks: high risk, low liquidity, and prone to sharp reversals.

shifts: This is the first live edition. Yesterday's file was a sample layout with no real picks, so no prior pick could have hit an invalidation level.
Versus Friday's risk-on close (+0.6-0.8% across indexes), sentiment is flat to cautious. Nasdaq futures lagged, and chips are leading lower.
Oil turned stronger: Brent is back above $106 (highest since Sept. 29) after weekend Houthi and tanker attacks, up from about $104 at Friday's close.
Crypto is weaker on the week: BTC is down about 4% and ETH about 7%, with nine straight days of ETH ETF outflows. Monday's moves are small (BTC -0.6%, ETH +0.9%).

crypto.note: 10-year yields above 5% and Fed hike risk are weighing on it. Spot ETFs took in $21M on Oct 9 after about $679M of outflows over the prior five sessions.
Spot ETFs have seen about $697M of outflows over nine straight days. Whale accumulation (~166K ETH) and Glamsterdam testnet progress offer some support.
Weakest top-10 coin last week on risk-off moves. SOL ETFs had outflows on six of seven October days; the Alpenglow mainnet is expected this month.
Institutional account controls went live on the XRP Ledger on Oct 9, but the price hasn't responded. It trades as a high-beta altcoin.
